branchName.commandInputTemplate:
{basePrompt}

Naming rules (override any conflicting style above):
- Format: <type>/<short-slug>, type is one of feat, fix, chore, refactor, docs, test, perf
- Lowercase kebab-case, 3–6 words, max 50 chars, only a-z 0-9 - /
- If the task mentions an issue or ticket number, put it first in the slug, e.g. fix/1234-token-refresh
- Describe the change, not the process

Task: {firstPrompt}

fixCommitFailure.commandInputTemplate:
{basePrompt}

Rules:
- Never use --no-verify, and don't edit or disable hooks, git config, identity, or signing.
- Only re-stage files that were already staged or changed by the fix. Never `git add -A`.
- Don't commit until I approve.

First state the cause and your proposed fix (file:line, or a corrected message for commit-msg hooks). Don't touch flagged secrets without asking. Wait for my OK.
After I approve, apply the fix, re-run the hook's commands, and show `git diff --cached --stat` plus the commit command. Don't run it.

fixPushFailure.commandInputTemplate:
{basePrompt}

Rules:
- Never use --no-verify, --force, or --force-with-lease unless I explicitly approve it.
- Don't edit or disable hooks, and don't change git config, credentials, or remotes.
- Don't retry the push until I approve.

First state the cause (hook, non-fast-forward, permissions, auth, server rejection) and your proposed fix. For auth or permission problems, tell me what to do instead of working around them. Wait for my OK.
After I approve, apply the fix, re-run the hook's commands locally, and show me the push command. Don't run it.

fixChecks.commandInputTemplate:
{basePrompt}

Rules:
- Read-only on GitHub/GitLab: no comments, no CI re-runs, no pushing, no commits unless I ask.
- Don't skip, disable, or loosen tests, lint rules, or type checks to make a check pass.

First give, per failing check: the root cause in one line and the proposed fix with file:line. Call out flaky or unrelated failures instead of changing code for them. Wait for my OK.
After I approve, apply the fix and run the same checks locally.

resolveConflicts.commandInputTemplate:
{basePrompt}

Rules:
- Do NOT push, force-push, or post anything on GitHub/GitLab.
- Do NOT run `git rebase --continue`, `git merge --continue`, or `git commit` until I approve.
- Never take "ours" or "theirs" for a whole file blindly.

First list each conflict: file:line, what each side changed, and your proposed resolution. Flag logic, schema/migration, lockfile, and config conflicts. Wait for my OK.
After I approve, apply the resolutions, regenerate lockfiles instead of hand-merging them, run build/tests, and show me the command to finish. Don't run it.

resolveComments.commandInputTemplate:
{basePrompt}

/grill-me

Rules:
- Do NOT reply to, resolve, react to, or post anything on GitHub/GitLab.
- Do NOT commit or push unless I ask.

Before editing, list each comment with file:line, what the reviewer wants, and your planned change (or why you'd push back). Then wait for my OK.
After I approve, make the changes, run relevant tests/lint, and end with a short reply per comment that I can paste myself.
